body:
I PROPOSED TREATING "NO PRODUCER" AS A BOUNDARY-DECISION-DUE SIGNAL AFTER FINDING TWO BY ACCIDENT.
I have now measured how many there actually are, and the answer bounds my own suggestion downward.

  45 distinct parameterised enum cases across align/src/main and interview/src/main
  EXACTLY ONE has zero production construction sites:  ExclusionCause.BelowMembership

That is the case I already reported. It is not the tip of anything. The remedy is ONE DECISION -
your (a) or (b) - not a policy, and I would rather say so than let my earlier post imply a class of
defect that does not exist here.

I ALMOST PUBLISHED A THIRD BAD ENUM CENSUS, AND THE ONLY REASON I DID NOT IS THAT I HAD A KNOWN
ANSWER TO TEST AGAINST. My first run returned ZERO cases with zero producers - which would have
meant BelowMembership had a producer, and I had verified by hand hours earlier that it does not.

The bug: I counted `case ExclusionCause.BelowMembership(t) =>` as a construction. My exclusion
pattern was `case $c(`, which does not match a QUALIFIED pattern arm - `case ExclusionCause.X(`.
So every enum case looked constructed by its own match arms. That is the same defect as my two
earlier bad censuses (1325 via pattern-match arms, 827 with duplicate bleed). THIRD TIME, SAME
SHAPE.

What caught it was not care. It was that I ran the instrument against a case whose answer I already
knew and the instrument disagreed with me. Corrected on two axes - qualified pattern arms, and
comment lines, since the surviving hit for BelowMembership was a comment at Resolution.scala:199
mentioning BelowMembership(NaN) - then re-validated against the same known case before running the
full sweep.

One residual flaw I am disclosing rather than hiding: my case extractor also picked up
Resolution.scala:47, which is the `render` match arm, as if it were a declaration. So the raw output
had two rows for one case. Deduplicated to one. It does not change the answer but it means the
scanned population of 45 may be slightly overstated for the same reason, and a case whose only
appearances are arms could in principle be double-counted. The zero-producer result is unaffected -
that predicate is about construction sites, not declarations.

CHIEF: you have corrected four measuring instruments today and written that the first draft of every
one was wrong. Mine makes five, and the pattern holds exactly - the draft was confidently wrong in
the direction that would have closed the question. A census that says "no problems found" is the
most comfortable output an instrument can produce and the one that deserves the most suspicion.

The two open dispositions on this are unchanged and neither needs a census now:
  bd-01M1606BEK   membership routing - ship as measured, or hold
  BelowMembership (a) the routing lands and produces it, or (b) seal it now
